annotations.title: It is a holie and healthful cogitation to pray for the dead.
annotations.text: The Catholique beleefe, doctrine, and practise of praying for the dead, [1] is so euidently confirmed by this place, that our aduersaries haue no better shift to auoide the same, then by denying these bookes to be Canonical Scripture. Which being authentically proued, [2] it may here suffice to adde that albeit the Greke text (as in other innumerable places) differeth from the Latin, yet it is no lesse clere for this doctrin. [3] Which in Englishe is thus: v. 45. Regarding (or considering) that grace is layde vp for them that sleepe (or dye) in pietie: to witte in true faith and repentance; in the next verse (46) inferreth thus: Wherupon he (Iudas Machabeus) made reconciliation (or expiation) for the dead, that they might be deliuered (or loosed) from their sinne, that is, from punishment for sinne. Omitting therfore multitude of other proofes, we wil here only cite two great Doctors, [4] who with others teach that the denial of this particular point of religion is a condemned heresie. [5] S. Augustin li. de Haresib. hær. 53. noteth this for a special heresie, saying: Aerians are named of one Aerius, who being a priest, and taking it greuously that he could not be ordained a Bishop, falling into the heresie of the Arrians, added some proper doctrines of his owne, saying: that we ought not to pray, nor offer sacrifice for the dead. Likewise S. Bernard, ser. 66 in Cantica: in plaine termes saith they are heretikes, which beleue not that there is purgatorie fire after death, but that the soule departing from the bodie, goeth forthwith either to rest or to damnation. Let them then (saith he) aske of him who saide: There is some sinne that shal not be forgeuen, neither in this world, nor in the future: [6]why he sayd this, if there remaine no remission, and purgation of sinne in the future world? He therfore aduiseth al to beware of such seducers, saying: See the detracters, see the dogges. They deride vs, because we baptize infantes: for that we pray for the dead. [7] It is also most worthie of consideration, that Iudas Machabeus, (who did this charitable act for his souldiars slaine in the holie warres) was the High priest, or chief Bishop of the Church at that time, and defender of true faith and Religion. Finally we may also obserue that he did not anie new thing, but practised the vsual custome of the whole Church. [8] For so it appeareth by their sette forme of Office for the dead, called HASCHABAH, that is, Rest, or prayer for rest, in their booke MAHZOR, translated and set forth by Bishop Genebrard, in the yeare of our Lord. 1569. Where are these expresse supplications. Requiescat anima ipsius in cubili suo: iaceat in pace: dormiat in pace. His (or her) soule rest in his bed: lye, and slepe in peace. Againe, Ye Angels of peace come forth to mete him. &c. [9] And that the Iewes this day vse to pray for the dead, is a clere thing, and confessed by Protestantes, namely Munsterus, and Fagius in their Annotations vpon the 14 of Deut. and M. Whitaker, in his first booke against F. Dureus, fol 81.

notes.text: This text is clear for praying for the dead.
Denial of this doctrine is heresie.
S. Augustin. ep. 61. ad Dulcit. l. 1. c. 23. de morib. li. de cura pro mort. c. 1. & Enchir. c. 110.
Judas was high priest when he caused prayers and sacrifice to be offered for the dead.
It was the general practice of the Church.
And is yet observed by the Jews.
